To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

α‐crystalin has a temperature dependent chaperon‐like activity towards insulin B chain and zetacrystalin, the chaperone activity increases with increase in temperature, the hydrophobic surface area of α‐crystalilin is exposed more at higher temperatures, the chaperon activity is more in the structurally perturbed form of α‐crstalilin.
the chaperonelike activity of α‐ crystallin is more pronounced at temperatures above 35°C.
the chaperon‐like activity of lens α‐crystellin towards the aggregation of a protein increases sharply at temperatures above 27°C and is completely inhibited at 41°C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structural features of α‐crystalin that are responsible for its chaperone‐ like activity.
the structural and functional properties of α‐crystalin, a major lens protein and the most important chaperone of the eye lens.
elucidating the structural basis of chaperone‐ like activity of α‐ crystallin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chaperonelike activity of α‐ crystallin is a consequence of its ability to expose its hydrophobic surface at higher temperatures.
the chaperonin activity of α‐ crystallin is a temperature‐dependent phenomenon.
α‐crystalin is a molecular chaperone with its activity being modulated by its structural state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chaperon‐like activity of the protein is a function of its structural stability.
α‐crystalin is a chaperone that is active only in its structurally unstable form.
the chaperoning function of α‐crystalin is more pronounced at elevated temperature and is also concentration dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chaperone activity of α‐ crystallin is more pronounced at higher temperatures.
α‐crystalin is not a chaperone at room temperature.
α‐crystalin is a temperature‐dependent chaperone, with a threshold temperature of about 30°C, above which it acquires its chaperone activity.
